correctness.rationale: PASS. Reconstructed the centered Itô variance equation and exact distinction between dissipative closure (all deterministic centered configurations) and an arbitrary scalar Markov observable. The linear p=0 identity D=2S, two-particle identity D=2^(p+1) S^((p+2)/2), and the one-dimensional three-particle fourth-power identity D=9S^2 follow from pair differences and the zero-sum Newton identity. For N>=4, matched-variance collinear configurations A=(-1,1,0,...) and B=(-1/sqrt2,-1/sqrt2,1/sqrt2,1/sqrt2,0,...) have strictly different dissipations for every p>0; independently checked the factored difference at N=4,5,7 and noninteger and integer powers. For N=3,d>=2, equilateral versus collinear centered shapes have different p>0 powers by strict Jensen/convexity. For N=3,d=1, the two zero-sum variance-matched triples reduce to a strictly convex exponential equation with only p=0,2. At q=1, N=3,d=1,p=2, the exact variance drift is (-9+2lambda/3)S^2 and variance bracket (4lambda/3)S^3; independent symbolic Itô transform f(S)=3/(lambda S) gives drift delta=2+27/lambda and squared diffusion coefficient 4Z. BESQ positive for delta>2, transition Z_t/t -> chi-square_delta, tS -> 3/(lambda chi-square_delta) in law; inverse moments r<delta/2 and mean limit 1/9 follow from gamma integrals. No almost-sure limit or full generic nonlinear-configuration closure claimed. Finite checks do not establish BESQ transience or all-parameter classification by themselves; those analytic arguments are separately reconstructed.
